summary: The recovered integral was described as lacking an elementary closed form. Its asymmetry disappears under x↦−x, leaving the classical Fourier transform of a quartic rational function. The resulting formula is exact for every real modulation parameter.
definitions: Let a∈R and I(a)=∫R cos²(ax)/[(1+ix²)(1+4^x)(1−ix²)]dx.
Write w(x)=1/(1+4^x); then w(x)+w(−x)=1.

example.calculation: I(0)=π/(2√2), while I(a)→π/(4√2) as|a|→∞. Differentiating under the integral twice is allowed since x²/(1+x⁴) is integrable, giving I″(0)=−π/√2. The third derivative cannot be justified by the same absolute-moment argument; the closed form indeed has an|a|³ term near zero.
